title.ar: مسار التطبيقات والتفسير (AI SL) — الموضوعات الخاصة

body.en: Applications and Interpretation SL emphasizes mathematical modelling, spatial partitioning, non-parametric correlation, numerical methods, and financial analysis. This chapter covers the syllabus components exclusive to the AI SL course.

label.en: ● Level 1 Foundation — Non-Parametric Correlation & Function Modelling

body.en:
Spearman's Rank Correlation Coefficient \(r_s\): A non-parametric measure of statistical dependence between the rankings of two variables. It assesses how well the relationship between two variables can be described using a monotonic function (not strictly linear):

\[ r_s = 1 - \frac{6\sum d_i^2}{n(n^2 - 1)}, \quad -1 \le r_s \le 1, \]

where \(d_i = \text{rank}(x_i) - \text{rank}(y_i)\) is the difference between the ranks of observation \(i\), and \(n\) is the sample size. When tied observations occur, assign each tied value the average (arithmetic mean) of the ranks they would have received.

Mathematical Modelling Selection:

  • Linear Model: \(y = mx + c\) — constant rate of increase/decrease.
  • Quadratic Model: \(y = ax^2 + bx + c\) — single extremum or parabolic trajectory.
  • Exponential Model: \(y = k a^x + c\) or \(y = k e^{rx} + c\) — proportional percentage growth or decay with horizontal asymptote \(y = c\).
  • Power Model: \(y = a x^b\) — transforms to linear \(\ln y = \ln a + b\ln x\).
  • Logistic Model: \(y = \frac{L}{1 + C e^{-kx}}\) — models constrained population growth asymptotically approaching carrying capacity \(L\).

label.en: ● Deep Conceptual Intuition — AI SL — Specific Topics

body.en: Proportional Invariance, Linear Structure & Quantitative Modeling: Across IB Diploma Mathematics: Analysis & Approaches / Applications & Interpretation SL, multi-step problems reduce to identifying invariant quantities—constant rates of change \(m = \dfrac{\Delta y}{\Delta x}\), conservation of total work/mass, or linear system rank conditions. A two-variable linear system \(a_1 x + b_1 y = c_1\), \(a_2 x + b_2 y = c_2\) has a unique intersection if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} \ne \dfrac{b_1}{b_2}\), no solution (parallel lines) if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{b_1}{b_2} \ne \dfrac{c_1}{c_2}\), and infinitely many solutions if all three ratios coincide.

label.en: ● Level 2 Analytical Tools — Voronoi Diagrams & Perpendicular Bisectors

body.en:
A Voronoi diagram partitions a 2D plane containing \(n\) distinct points \(S_1, S_2, \dots, S_n\) (called sites) into \(n\) convex polygonal cells. Every point within \(\text{Cell}(S_i)\) is closer to site \(S_i\) than to any other site:

\[ \text{Cell}(S_i) = \{ P \in \mathbb{R}^2 \mid d(P, S_i) \le d(P, S_j) \;\forall j \neq i \}. \]

Geometric Construction of Edges:

  • The boundary edge separating two adjacent cells \(\text{Cell}(A)\) and \(\text{Cell}(B)\) lies on the perpendicular bisector of segment \(AB\).
  • Midpoint: \[ M = \left(\frac{x_1 + x_2}{2}, \frac{y_1 + y_2}{2}\right). \]
  • Gradient of \(AB\): \(m_{AB} = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\). Gradient of perpendicular bisector: \[ m_{\perp} = -\frac{1}{m_{AB}} = -\frac{x_2 - x_1}{y_2 - y_1}. \]
  • Perpendicular bisector equation: \[ y - y_M = m_{\perp}(x - x_M). \]
  • Voronoi Vertices: The intersection of three or more edges. A Voronoi vertex is the circumcentre of the triangle formed by the three corresponding sites, and is equidistant from all three.
  • Largest Empty Circle (Toxic Waste Problem): The optimal position for a new site or hazardous facility farthest from all existing sites must be located either at a Voronoi vertex or along the boundary of the region.

label.en: ● Level 3 University Rigor — Numerical Integration & Annuity Mathematics

body.en:
The Trapezoidal Rule: When an analytical antiderivative cannot be expressed in closed form or data is given at discrete intervals, the definite integral \(\int_a^b f(x)\,dx\) is approximated by partitioning \([a, b]\) into \(n\) equal subintervals of width \(h = \frac{b - a}{n}\):

\[ \int_a^b f(x)\,dx \approx \frac{h}{2} \left[ y_0 + 2(y_1 + y_2 + \dots + y_{n-1}) + y_n \right], \]

where \(y_i = f(a + i h)\). Error behaviour: if \(f''(x) > 0\) (concave up), chords lie above the curve, so the trapezoidal rule overestimates the true area; if \(f''(x) < 0\) (concave down), chords lie below the curve, so it underestimates the true area.

Annuity & Amortization Theory: An annuity is a sequence of equal payments \(PMT\) made at equal intervals. The present value of an ordinary annuity compounded at interest rate \(r\) per period for \(N\) periods is derived from a geometric series:

\[ PV = PMT \left[ \frac{1 - (1 + r)^{-N}}{r} \right]. \]

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (AI SL — Specific Topics)

body.en:
Why Successive Multipliers & Harmonic Average Speed Work: If a quantity \(Q_0\) undergoes a percentage change \(p\%\) followed by \(q\%\), the compound multiplier is the product of individual scale factors:

\[ Q_{\text{final}} = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)\!\left(1 + \frac{q}{100}\right) = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p + q}{100} + \frac{pq}{10000}\right) \]

Notice the cross term \(\dfrac{pq}{10000}\): an increase of \(p\%\) followed by a decrease of \(p\%\) yields \(Q_0\bigl(1 - (p/100)^2\bigr) < Q_0\). Similarly, traveling equal distance \(d\) at speeds \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) takes total time \(T = \frac{d}{v_1} + \frac{d}{v_2}\), so average speed is the harmonic mean \(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2d}{d/v_1 + d/v_2} = \dfrac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

label.en: Worked Example AI.1 — Spearman's Rank Correlation with Tied Ranks

problem.en:
Five students received the following test scores in Mathematics (X) and Physics (Y):
Math (X): 65, 80, 80, 50, 92
Physics (Y): 70, 85, 75, 60, 90
Calculate Spearman's rank correlation coefficient \(r_s\) and interpret the result.

solution.en:
1. Rank variable \(X\) in descending order (highest score gets rank 1):
92: rank 1; 80, 80: tied for ranks 2 and 3 \(\implies \frac{2 + 3}{2} = 2.5\); 65: rank 4; 50: rank 5.
Ranks of \(X\): 4, 2.5, 2.5, 5, 1.

2. Rank variable \(Y\) in descending order:
90: rank 1; 85: rank 2; 75: rank 3; 70: rank 4; 60: rank 5.
Ranks of \(Y\): 4, 2, 3, 5, 1.

3. Calculate rank differences \(d_i = \text{rank}(X) - \text{rank}(Y)\) and \(d_i^2\):
Student 1: \(d_1 = 4 - 4 = 0 \implies d_1^2 = 0\)
Student 2: \(d_2 = 2.5 - 2 = 0.5 \implies d_2^2 = 0.25\)
Student 3: \(d_3 = 2.5 - 3 = -0.5 \implies d_3^2 = 0.25\)
Student 4: \(d_4 = 5 - 5 = 0 \implies d_4^2 = 0\)
Student 5: \(d_5 = 1 - 1 = 0 \implies d_5^2 = 0\)
Sum: \(\sum d_i^2 = 0 + 0.25 + 0.25 + 0 + 0 = 0.5\).

4. Compute \(r_s\) with \(n = 5\):
\[ r_s = 1 - \frac{6(0.5)}{5(5^2 - 1)} = 1 - \frac{3}{5(24)} = 1 - \frac{3}{120} = 1 - 0.025 = 0.975. \]

Conclusion: \(r_s = 0.975\) indicates a very strong positive monotonic relationship between mathematics and physics performance.

label.en: Worked Example AI.2 — Constructing Voronoi Edges and Vertices

problem.en:
Three mobile transmission towers are located at \(A(1, 2)\), \(B(5, 4)\), and \(C(3, 8)\).
(a) Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of segment \(AB\).
(b) Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of segment \(BC\).
(c) Find the coordinates of the Voronoi vertex formed by the intersection of these bisectors.

solution.en:
(a) Perpendicular bisector of \(AB\):
Midpoint \(M_{AB} = \left( \frac{1 + 5}{2}, \frac{2 + 4}{2} \right) = (3, 3)\).
Gradient \(m_{AB} = \frac{4 - 2}{5 - 1} = \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}\).
Perpendicular gradient \(m_1 = -\frac{1}{1/2} = -2\).
Equation: \(y - 3 = -2(x - 3) \implies y = -2x + 9\).

(b) Perpendicular bisector of \(BC\):
Midpoint \(M_{BC} = \left( \frac{5 + 3}{2}, \frac{4 + 8}{2} \right) = (4, 6)\).
Gradient \(m_{BC} = \frac{8 - 4}{3 - 5} = \frac{4}{-2} = -2\).
Perpendicular gradient \(m_2 = -\frac{1}{-2} = \frac{1}{2}\).
Equation: \(y - 6 = \frac{1}{2}(x - 4) \implies y = \frac{1}{2}x + 4\).

(c) Intersect the two perpendicular bisectors:
\[ -2x + 9 = \frac{1}{2}x + 4 \implies 5 = 2.5x \implies x = 2. \]
Substitute \(x = 2\): \(y = -2(2) + 9 = 5\).
The Voronoi vertex is at \((2, 5)\).
Verify distance to \(A, B, C\):
\(d(V, A) = \sqrt{(2-1)^2 + (5-2)^2} = \sqrt{1 + 9} = \sqrt{10}\).
\(d(V, B) = \sqrt{(2-5)^2 + (5-4)^2} = \sqrt{9 + 1} = \sqrt{10}\).
\(d(V, C) = \sqrt{(2-3)^2 + (5-8)^2} = \sqrt{1 + 9} = \sqrt{10}\).
All three distances are exactly \(\sqrt{10}\), confirming \((2, 5)\) is the circumcentre.

label.en: ⚠ AI SL Exam Traps: Tied Ranks, Bisector Slopes & TVM Solver Signs

body.en:
Tied Ranks Assignment: If two candidates tie for rank 3, both receive rank 3.5, and the next candidate receives rank 5 (NOT 4). Forgetting to skip ranks when ties occur invalidates the Spearman formula.

Negative Reciprocal Gradient: For perpendicular bisectors, always take the negative reciprocal: \(m_{\perp} = -\frac{1}{m}\). A frequent sign error is forgetting the minus sign, leading to bisectors parallel to the segment.

GDC TVM Sign Convention: Money paid out (deposits, investments) must be entered as negative (-PV or -PMT); money received (withdrawals, loan principal received) must be entered as positive. Confusing signs triggers "ERROR: DOMAIN" on the calculator.

Worked Example (AI SL Paper 2 — 8 marks):
Three mobile towers are located at \(A(1, 5)\), \(B(7, 3)\), and \(C(5, 9)\) on a coordinate grid (\(1\text{ unit} = 1\text{ km}\)).
(a) Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of \([AB]\) in the form \(y = mx + c\). [4]
(b) The Voronoi vertex is \(V(4.5, 5.5)\). A fourth tower is to be placed at \(V\). Calculate the distance from \(V\) to tower \(A\) and explain the significance of this distance. [4]

Official IB Markscheme Solution:
(a) Midpoint of \([AB]\): \(M = \left(\frac{1+7}{2}, \frac{5+3}{2}\right) = (4, 4)\) [A1]
Gradient \(m_{AB} = \frac{3 - 5}{7 - 1} = -\frac{2}{6} = -\frac{1}{3} \implies m_\perp = 3\) [M1] [A1]
Line equation: \(y - 4 = 3(x - 4) \implies y = 3x - 8\) [A1]
(b) Distance \(VA = \sqrt{(4.5 - 1)^2 + (5.5 - 5)^2} = \sqrt{12.25 + 0.25} = \sqrt{12.5} \approx 3.54\text{ km}\) [M1] [A1]
Significance: \(V\) is equidistant (\(3.54\text{ km}\) from \(A\), \(B\), and \(C\), representing the centre of the largest empty circle (the point furthest from any existing tower where signal coverage is weakest) [R1] [A1]

rows.en: The \(25\%\) reduction applies to the larger base \(1.25 Q_0\), not \(Q_0\).
Dividing by a negative number reverses order on the real number line.
Flip the inequality symbol whenever multiplying or dividing by a negative: \(x < -4\).
Computing round-trip average speed as \(\frac{v_1 + v_2}{2}\)
Time spent at the slower speed is longer than time spent at the faster speed.
Use total distance over total time: \(v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

question.en:
Practice AI.2: A company takes out a loan of $120,000 to purchase equipment at an annual interest rate of 6% compounded monthly, repayable by equal monthly payments over 10 years.
(a) Find the amount of each monthly payment.
(b) Calculate the total interest paid over the life of the loan.
question.ar:
Practice AI.2: A company takes out a loan of $120,000 to purchase equipment at an annual interest rate of 6% compounded monthly, repayable by equal monthly payments over 10 years.
(a) أوجد amount of each monthly payment.
(b) احسب total interest paid over the lإذا كانe of the loan.

solution.en:
(a) Use the annuity formula or TVM solver:
Number of payments \(N = 10 \times 12 = 120\).
Monthly interest rate \(r = \frac{0.06}{12} = 0.005\).
\[ PV = PMT \left[ \frac{1 - (1 + r)^{-N}}{r} \right] \implies 120,000 = PMT \left[ \frac{1 - (1.005)^{-120}}{0.005} \right]. \]
Compute discount factor: \(1 - (1.005)^{-120} = 1 - 0.549633 = 0.450367\).
Factor / 0.005 \(= 90.07345\).
\[ PMT = \frac{120,000}{90.07345} \approx \$1,332.25. \]

(b) Total amount paid: 120 \times 1332.25 = $159,870.
Total interest: \(\\(159,870 - \)120,000 = \$39,870\).

solution.en: In a Voronoi diagram, the boundary edge between two sites is along the perpendicular bisector of the line segment connecting them. 1. Find the midpoint \(M\) of the segment \(AB\): \[ M = \left(\frac{2 + 6}{2}, \frac{4 + 2}{2}\right) = (4, 3) \] 2. Find the gradient of segment \(AB\): \[ m_{AB} = \frac{2 - 4}{6 - 2} = \frac{-2}{4} = -\frac{1}{2} \] 3. The gradient of the perpendicular bisector is the negative reciprocal of \(m_{AB}\): \[ m_{\perp} = -\frac{1}{-\frac{1}{2}} = 2 \] 4. Use the point-slope form with midpoint \((4, 3)\) and gradient \(m_{\perp} = 2\): \[ y - 3 = 2(x - 4) \implies y = 2x - 8 + 3 \implies y = 2x - 5 \] Common Misconceptions: - Choice B uses the gradient of \(AB\) rather than its negative reciprocal. - Choice C correctly finds the gradient \(m = 2\) but forgets to add the \(y\)-coordinate of the midpoint, setting \(y = 2(x - 4) = 2x - 8\). - Choice D uses \(m = -2\) instead of \(+2\).

question.en: Consider the functions \( f(x) = x^2 - 6x + 11 \) and \( g(x) = 2x - 1 \). The graphs of these functions intersect at two points. One of the intersection points is \( (2, 3) \). Find the x-coordinate of the other intersection point.
question.ar: Consider the functions \( f(x) = x^2 - 6x + 11 \) and \( g(x) = 2x - 1 \). The graphs of these functions intersect at two points. One of the intersection points is \( (2, 3) \). أوجد x-coordinate of the other intersection point.

hints.en: To find the intersection points of the two functions, we set \( f(x) = g(x) \). \( x^2 - 6x + 11 = 2x - 1 \).

We are looking for two numbers that multiply to 12 and add to -8. These numbers are -6 and -2. \( (x - 2)(x - 6) = 0 \) This gives us two possible solutions for x: \( x = 2 \) or \( x = 6 \).
